newsitem.title: UK: Halifax set to hand out basic 200 shares.
newsitem.headline: Halifax set to hand out basic 200 shares.

text.p: Britain's Halifax Building Society said on Friday it expected to distribute some 2.675 billion shares in its planned float among about 8.0 million members who qualify as either borrowers or investors, or both.
Graham Johnston, deputy general manager of the society, told Reuters the basic distribution of shares to all who qualify on the basis of time would be 200 shares.

Investors with more than 1,000 pounds ($1,689) in their accounts on specific qualifying dates would qualify for a further variable distribution of shares based on one additional share per 50 stg over the threshold.

The Halifax has 6.7 million investing members and 2.0 million borrowing members. Of these, there is an overlap 0.7 million which means that the Society is sending out a total of around 8.0 million voting packs.
At its special general meeting on February 24, over 50 percent of the investing members must vote in favour of the proposal or it will fail.

Investing members will also get a variable share allocation depending on how much money they have in their accounts on particular dates, this will range from 200 shares to a maximum of 1,181 for those with 50,000 pounds ($84,430) or more.

"It is a big voting requirement," said Halifax assistant general manager Graham Johnston; "50 percent is a higher hurdle than others have faced...we're very confident we'll get it." The Halifax chief executive Mike Blackburn said the flotation was the largest ever single extension of share ownership in the UK and urged members to vote in favour. ($1=.5922 Pound)
